import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.preprocessing import PowerTransformer

# Dataset with both positive and negative values
np.random.seed(42)
data = {
    'returns': np.random.normal(0, 5, 50),
    'temperature_change': np.random.normal(2, 8, 50),
    'profit_loss': np.random.normal(-100, 500, 50)
}
df = pd.DataFrame(data)

# Verify data contains negative values (Box-Cox would fail)
print("Contains negative values:", (df < 0).any().any())

# Apply Yeo-Johnson transform using PowerTransformer from sklearn
pt = PowerTransformer(method='yeo-johnson', standardize=True)
df_yeojohnson = pd.DataFrame(
    pt.fit_transform(df),
    columns=df.columns
)

# Compare skewness before and after transformation
print("\nSkewness BEFORE Yeo-Johnson:")
for col in df.columns:
    print(f"  {col}: {stats.skew(df[col]):.3f}")

print("\nSkewness AFTER Yeo-Johnson:")
for col in df_yeojohnson.columns:
    print(f"  {col}: {stats.skew(df_yeojohnson[col]):.3f}")

# Print the transformed data and lambda values
print("\nLambda values:", pt.lambdas_)
print("\nTransformed data (first 5 rows):")
print(df_yeojohnson.head())
